messages:
Maria: FYI — after the kernel-selector v2 change we landed this morning I'm seeing a rise in 95th p50 token latency on L4 and A10 for medium-length requests (~512 tokens). Samples from canary: a10: p95 gen latency +18%, l4: +12%. Perf traces attached below.
Ben: ugh. which path is picking now? new kernel or falling back to generic?
Maria: selector is choosing the fused-kv-v2 path for many workloads. aggregate shows increased kernel stalls on KV reloads. stack traces: `kernel: fused-kv-v2`, `kv_fragmentation_rate: 0.32`, `avg_kv_reload_ms: 4.8`
AJ: interesting. that path reduced mem copies but introduced more short-lived KV reloads when batch shapes vary. Did we change batching heuristics too?
Maria: yes — continuous-batching updated to be more aggressive about filling  tokens up to new max_tokens_per_batch=16384. Previously it favored smaller batches.
Kai: so we're packing more tokens into a single batch which increases KV churn?
Maria: exactly. More mixed lengths => more KV fragment eviction and reloads. perf-bot flamegraphs attached.
Olivia: can you paste the profiler output (nvprof / Nsight summary)? even coarse numbers help.
Maria: pasted excerpt:
```
GPU: A10
kernel_time_ms fused-kv-v2: 9.4
kernel_time_ms generic-attn: 6.8
kv_reload_count: 182
avg_kv_reload_ms: 4.8
p95_end_to_end_ms: 138
```
```
GPU: L4
kernel_time_ms fused-kv-v2: 7.1
kernel_time_ms generic-attn: 5.9
kv_reload_count: 140
avg_kv_reload_ms: 3.9
p95_end_to_end_ms: 116
```
Ben: hmm, fused-kv-v2 is slower on these mixes. maybe it excels for long contiguous sequences but not for many short prefix variations.
AJ: Workaround: tighten max_tokens_per_batch for A10 and L4 so we avoid packing cross-shape batches that trigger reloads. Also consider a small heuristic: prefer kernel fallback to generic-attn when kv_fragmentation_rate > 0.2.
Kai: what values do you propose?
AJ: propose: A10 max_tokens_per_batch -> 12288 (from 16384), L4 -> 12288, H100/A100 keep at 16384. T4 remain at 8192. Also temp disable fused-kv-v2 on A10 for canary.
Olivia: can we simulate with the queue replay harness quickly? I can run a 6-hour replay with mixed client traces.
Maria: I ran a 30m replay earlier; toggling A10 to 12k reduced kv_reload_count by ~45% and p95 by ~11%.
perf-bot: perf regression check run #214: after change -> p95 reduced from 138ms to 122ms for A10 on sample workload.
Ben: good signal. next steps?
Maria: 1) schedule canary config: set per-gpu max_tokens map: {A10:12288, L4:12288, T4:8192, A100:16384, H100:16384}. 2) add selector rule: if kv_fragmentation_rate > 0.25 prefer generic-attn fallback. 3) run 6h replay (Olivia). 4) collect telemetry for 48h and revert if SLO regressions elsewhere.
Kai: one more: log a new metric `batch_shape_entropy` to help detect harmful mixes early.
AJ: agreed. also leave rollout behind feature flag so we can A/B quickly.
Olivia: I'll queue the replay and canary this afternoon. ping me if you want me to include heavy short-seq traffic.
Maria: thanks. I'll prepare a short runbook for oncall: what to look for and how to rollback the per-gpu map.
Ben: +1. let's try the conservative per-gpu ceilings for now. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled by Olivia at 2026-03-18T16:30Z for config change `max_tokens_per_batch: per-gpu-map-v3`
Maria: noting for post-mortem: kernel-selector needs a heatmap test combining kernel fit and kv_fragmentation to avoid global regressions.
AJ: I'll add a perf test in CI that runs the selector against a small corpus of mixed-length prompts. low-cost but should catch this class.
Olivia: started 6h replay job (job_id: replay-20260318-01). will post results to this thread when done.
Maria: thanks everyone. short-term fix looks good; long-term we'll need a better cost model in selector that accounts for KV reload overhead.
